obligations.name: typed product replay
obligations.evidence: 279000 toy product collisions and 4 P-256 coordinate equations replay with zero failures.
obligations.scope: Complete order-five control and deterministic scalar-labelled P-256 witnesses.

obligations.name: linked-coordinate independence
obligations.evidence: The linked pair has rank one over both fields and both row orders.

obligations.name: independent-coordinate net information

obligations.scope: Direct product of two independent cyclic-group coordinates.

obligations.name: known-label selector cost
obligations.evidence: The optimistic generic product collision costs 2^255.825748 samples per useful original row and is 2^127.947236 times original rho.
obligations.scope: Uniform balanced generic product collision; projection, not a measured attack.

obligations.name: non-homomorphic coupling
obligations.evidence: No map supplies two independent rows on the original recovery variables without adding unknowns or a product-size collision space.
obligations.scope: Mechanisms outside homomorphic, independent-block, and known-label cases.

controls: Complete toy census: 961 profile pairs, 7447750 pair tests, 1441500 first-coordinate collisions, and 279000 full product collisions.
P-256 controls materialize 17 primary and two sets of auxiliary points, replay four equations, and rank all systems over two fields in both row orders.
Rounds 39, 302, 303, and 307 are imported only after exact byte-hash, schema, curve, factor-base, conclusion, and boundary checks.
cost_accounting: Measured: complete toy state and pair enumeration, collision/replay counts, P-256 scalar multiplications, group additions, dual-field rank operations, process telemetry, and artifact sizes.
Modeled lower bound: uniform simultaneous-negation product birthday collision at 2^255.825748 samples; this is explicitly not measurement.
Storage alternatives are separated: an 82-byte materialized record list fails the storage gate, while a constant-memory walk can pass storage but retains the order-n operation exponent.
Unset: a non-homomorphic coupling, actual relation yield, product-system degree, decomposition, sparse linear algebra, target recovery, and complete attack cost.
exploration_boundary: Exact for direct linked, independent-block, and known-label product lifts in prime-order cyclic groups; not a universal theorem about non-homomorphic encodings or higher algebraic correspondences.
weakest_open_obligation: Construct a typed non-homomorphic event whose two replayed equations both survive projection to the original P-256 recovery variables, add no unresolved log block, and cost no more than original-group rho.
narrowest_supported_finding: A direct two-coordinate product lift does not yield two useful original-system rows: linked coordinates collapse to rank one, while independent coordinates add an unknown block and a generic full collision costs order n rather than order sqrt(n).
